4. Record shows that in respect of an incident, which is alleged to have occurred on 12.07.2023, a delayed FIR dated 13.07.2023 was lodged by first informant-Hakikullah (father of the prosecutrix)
and was registered as Case Crime No. 154 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366 IPC, Police Station-Dumariyaganj, District-Siddharth Nagar.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: In the aforesaid FIR, applicant-Abdul Salam has been nominated as solitary named accused.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: 6. The gravamen of the allegations made in the FIR is to the effect that named accused Abdul Salam enticed away the minor daughter of first informant i.e. the prosecutrix namely X aged about 16 years.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: 7. After above-mentioned FIR was lodged, Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of concerned case crime number in terms of Chapter-XII Cr.P.C.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: The prosecutrix was recovered on 16.07.2023.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: The prosecutrix in her aforesaid statement has not supported the FIR.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: The prosecutrix has further stated that she readily and willingly joined the applicant and thereafter accompanied him to various places.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: However, the prosecutrix has categorically stated that no physical relations were established between the parties.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: Subsequent to above, the prosecutrix was requested for her internal medical examination.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: The prosecutrix in her statement before the Doctor, who medically examined her, has rejoined her previous statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. but with the improvement that physical relations between the parties were established on numerous occasions.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: The Doctor, who medically examined the prosecutrix, did not find any such signs on her body so as to denote commission of deliberate or forceful sexual assault.

sentences.text:
However, with regard to the private part of the prosecutrix, the Doctor has opined as follows:-
"Hymen - Old, Torn, Healed tags"
8.

sentences.text: As per the medical opinion, the prosecutrix was said to be aged about 17 years.

sentences.text: The occurrence giving rise to present criminal proceedings is alleged to have occurred on 12.07.2023.

sentences.text: As such, the prosecutrix was aged about 15 years, 2 months and 11 days on the date of occurrence.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant contends that though the applicant is named as well as charge sheeted accused yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: Referring to the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161/164 Cr.P.C., he submits that the prosecutrix is a willing and consenting party.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: The prosecutrix out of her own sweet-will joined the applicant and thereafter, accompanied him to various places.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: As such, no offence under Sections 363, 366 IPC can be said to have been committed by applicant as the prosecutrix was neither abducted, kidnapped or enticed away by the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: In her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix has categorically stated that no physical relations were established between the parties.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: In her subsequent statement under Sections 164 Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix has remained silent regarding commission of sexual assault.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: He, therefore, contends that since the prosecutrix in her statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has not alleged that applicant is guilty of committing aggravated sexual assault or penetrative sexual assault upon the prosecutrix, therefore, no offence under Sections 5/6 POCSO Act can be said to have made out against applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: As such, applicant is liable to be admitted to bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: 11. Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as, he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: Applicant is in jail since 16.07.2023.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: As such, he has undergone more than 5 months of incarceration.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: The police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: As such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallized.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: However, up to this stage, no such circumstance has emerged on record necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: On the above premise, he submits that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: In case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: 12. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. and the learned counsel representing first informant have opposed the present application for bail.

They contend that the prosecutrix is a young girl and was aged about 15 years, 2 months and 11 days on the date of occurrence, therefore, the consent, if any,
of the prosecutrix is wholly immaterial.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Salam vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023.json

sentences.text:
The fact that modesty of the prosecutrix was dislodged is clearly established by the opinion expressed by the Doctor, who medically examined the prosecutrix,
qua her private parts.

sentences.text:
Since the prosecutrix was below 16 years of age on the date of occurrence,
therefore, her consent, if any, in joining the applicant is wholly immaterial.

sentences.text: In support of above, the learned A.G.A. and the learned counsel representing first informant have referred to the judgment of Supreme Court in X (Minor) Vs. The State of Jharkhand and Another 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 194.
